plan: My value is $13. I want to win if and only if the price is less than or equal to my value. I should bid my value in the sealed bid stage. This way, I will stay in the ascending clock auction until the clock reaches my value. If the second highest bid is less than or equal to my value, then I win. If the second highest bid is more than my value, then I lose, which is what I want.

[I should bid slightly below my value to ensure I win when the other bidders have lower values and to avoid overpaying significantly if they have higher values. I will bid $8.9, which is slightly below my value of $9. This allows me to win if the other bidders have values less than $9, and I exit if the clock reaches $8.9. If the other bidders have values greater than $9, I will lose but will not overpay. ]

[My value is $8. I want to maximize my profit. In the ascending clock auction, I want to stay in as long as the price is less than my value. If I bid my value, and another bidder bids higher, I will lose, which is fine. If I bid lower than my value, I might win at a lower price, but I might also exit too early and miss out on potential profit. Therefore, I will bid my true value of $8. This will ensure I stay in the auction as long as the price is below my value, maximizing potential profit.]
